title: DNS and the CDN
summary: The first two hops of every request: DNS with its TTLs, latency routing and health-checked failover, then the CDN edge with cache keys, Cache-Control, stale-while-revalidate, origin shield and purges.

steps.title: The path in front of your servers
body: Before a request reaches your code it passes through several layers, each of which can cache, route or fail:
```text
browser / app
| 1. DNS: shop.example.com -> which address?   (cached for the TTL)
v
CDN edge (near the user)   2. cached? answer in ~10-30 ms : else go to the origin
v
load balancer (your region)   3. pick a healthy server
v
app servers -> caches, databases, queues
**DNS** answers carry a **TTL**: resolvers and clients cache the answer for that many seconds. DNS can route:
- **Latency-based or geo routing**: answer with the region closest to the user.
- **Weighted**: send 5% of lookups to a new region.
- **Health-checked failover**: stop handing out an address whose health check fails.
DNS failover is slow and leaky: the change takes effect only as cached answers expire, some resolvers and
clients keep answers longer than the TTL, and long-lived connections never look again. Short TTLs (30 to 60 s)
help but cost more lookups. Use DNS to steer between regions; use load balancers for fast failover inside one.

prompt: Region A fails. The DNS health check runs every 30 s and marks an endpoint down after 3 failures in a row.
The record's TTL is 300 s. Roughly how long until **most** users are sent to region B?
options: Up to about 6.5 minutes: 90 s to detect, then up to 300 s for cached answers to expire, and a tail that takes longer
Immediately: DNS updates are pushed to every client
About 90 seconds: detection is the only delay
explain: Detection (3 x 30 s) plus the TTL (300 s) is the worst case for well-behaved resolvers. Some clients cache
longer or hold open connections, so a tail of traffic keeps hitting region A. That is why multi-region
designs lower the TTL ahead of time and still expect stragglers.

steps.title: The CDN and Cache-Control
body: A **CDN** keeps copies of responses at edge locations near users. A hit is fast and costs your origin nothing.
The origin decides what may be cached with response headers:
| Header directive | Meaning for a shared cache (the CDN) |
| `max-age=600` | fresh for 600 s (browsers and shared caches) |
| `s-maxage=60` | fresh for 60 s in **shared** caches only; overrides `max-age` there |
| `private` | only the user's own browser may store it, never the CDN |
| `no-store` | nobody may store it |
| `no-cache` | may be stored, but must be revalidated with the origin before each use |
| `stale-while-revalidate=30` | after expiry, serve the stale copy for up to 30 s while refreshing in the background |
| `stale-if-error=600` | serve a stale copy for up to 600 s if the origin is failing |
| `immutable` | the content never changes at this URL: do not even revalidate |

- **Cache key**: what the CDN uses to decide two requests are "the same" (by default the URL; often plus some headers or cookies). Every extra part in the key splits the cache and lowers the hit rate.
- **Origin shield**: a middle tier of CDN caches, so a miss in 200 edge locations becomes one request to your origin, not 200.
- **Purge**: telling the CDN to drop a cached object early. It takes time to reach every edge: prefer versioned URLs (`app.3f9a1c.js`) with a one-year `max-age` and `immutable`.

steps.prompt: Match each Cache-Control directive to its effect on the CDN.
pairs: The CDN may serve it for 60 s, whatever `max-age` says
The CDN must not store it; the browser may
Serve the old copy for 30 s while fetching a fresh one
Never revalidate: the URL's content will not change

steps.prompt: Which responses should the CDN cache?
buckets: Do not cache at the edge
items: A public price list sent with `s-maxage=60`
A response that sets a session cookie
steps.explain: Public, identical-for-everyone content belongs at the edge. Anything per user, any write, and anything that sets a cookie must not be cached there: caching it can show one user's data to another.

steps.prompt: Worst-case seconds before a failed region stops getting new lookups from a well-behaved resolver. What does this print?
steps.explain: 30 s to notice plus 60 s for the cached answer to expire. A TTL of 60 instead of 300 cuts the worst case from 330 to 90 s.

steps.prompt: Headers for a versioned JavaScript bundle that must be cached for a year and never revalidated.
steps.explain: 31,536,000 s is 365 days. `immutable` tells browsers not to revalidate on reload. This only works because a new release gets a new file name.

prompt: **Bug report after a release.** Some users see the new HTML but the old JavaScript, and the page breaks.
The bundle is served as `/static/app.js` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`. What is the fix?
options: Put a content hash in the file name (`app.3f9a1c.js`) and reference it from the HTML, which itself gets a short TTL
Purge the CDN after every release and hope it reaches every edge in time
explain: The same URL served two different files. Versioned names make each release a new URL, so old and new copies
can never mix and you can cache for a year. Purging and short TTLs still leave a window; `no-store` throws away

steps.title: How long may the CDN keep it?
prompt: Write `int? EdgeTtl(string cacheControl)`: how many seconds a **shared cache** may serve a response, from its
`Cache-Control` header value. Directives are separated by commas; ignore spaces and case. Rules, in this order:
5. otherwise -> `null` (no explicit freshness; we do not guess).
Careful: `s-maxage` and `max-age` are different directive names. `EdgeTtl("s-maxage=60, max-age=0")` is `60`.
solution: if (directives.TryGetValue("s-maxage", out var s) && int.TryParse(s, out var sv)) return sv;
if (directives.TryGetValue("max-age", out var m) && int.TryParse(m, out var mv)) return mv;
hints: Split on `,`, then `Trim()` and `ToLowerInvariant()` each part. Split each part at the first `=` into a name and a value.
Keep the names in a `Dictionary<string, string>` and check the rules in order. `int.TryParse` reads the number.
template: Dojo.Eq("s-maxage wins for the CDN", (int?)60, EdgeTtl("s-maxage=60, max-age=0"));
Dojo.Eq("private is never at the edge", (int?)null, EdgeTtl("private, max-age=600"));
Dojo.Eq("case and spaces do not matter", (int?)30, EdgeTtl("  Max-Age=30 "));
Dojo.Eq("other directives are ignored", (int?)120, EdgeTtl("max-age=120 , stale-while-revalidate=30"));
